description: A lipid is any of a diverse group of small biological molecules that are hydrophobic or amphipathic; their chemical structures vary widely, so the category is held together by how its members behave in water rather than by a shared backbone.<sup class="fn" data-fn="1"></sup> The simplest are fatty acids, long hydrocarbon chains whose nonpolar bonds cannot interact with water, and cells put lipids to three principal uses: storing energy as fats, building membranes from phospholipids, and carrying chemical signals.<sup class="fn" data-fn="2"></sup> Modern surveys of cellular lipid composition find hundreds to thousands of distinct species differing in head group, chain length and degree of unsaturation, and why so many are maintained remains unsettled.<sup class="fn" data-fn="3"></sup>
